name: notepadia-bug-report
auditedRef: main @ f800ff7 ("feat(updater): offer updates in a Check for Updates dialog")
auditMethod: Static read of extensions/notepadia/src (browser, common, electron-main) plus the unit tests in extensions/notepadia/test, targeting only untested or weakly-tested paths. Item BUG-001 was additionally reproduced by executing the compiled module from lib/common under Node.
scope: extensions/notepadia/src (product-specific Notepadia code). Theia / @theia packages are treated as third party and out of scope.

schema.bug: What is wrong and what the user-visible consequence is.
schema.line_number: 1-based line in `file` where the defect lives.
schema.proposed_fix: The concrete code change that removes the defect.

priorityLevels.high: Wrong or unsafe behavior on a normal path; data loss, path escape, or a crash.
priorityLevels.medium: Wrong behavior on an edge or failure path, or a resource/leak that grows over time.
priorityLevels.low: Latent defect guarded by lucky defaults, a cosmetic mismatch, or a heuristic that is acceptable for now.

bugs.bug: resolveRenameTarget misses backslash path traversal. The `..` guard splits the typed name on '/' only, so on Windows a name like `..\evil.txt` survives as a single segment and is accepted. The result is a rename that moves the file OUT of its own folder while File > Rename claims it cannot. A UNC path (`\\server\share\a.txt`) is also accepted because the absolute-path check only rejects a leading '/' and drive letters. Reproduced: resolveRenameTarget('/ws/a.txt', '..\\evil.txt') -> {ok:true, path:'/ws/..\evil.txt'}.
bugs.proposed_fix: Normalize separators before parsing and refuse a leading backslash: `const normalized = typed.replace(/\\/g, '/');` then reject `normalized.startsWith('/')` (covering UNC and root) and run the existing empty/'.'/'..'/segment logic on `normalized`. Update the '/ws/a.txt' + '..\evil.txt' and UNC cases in test/file-operations.test.cjs to assert ok:false.

bugs.bug: The Ctrl+F / Ctrl+H document keydown listener is registered inside registerEditorKeybindings(), which is retried from its own catch block (and from onStart). Every retry that gets past the StandaloneKeybindingService check adds ANOTHER capture-phase 'keydown' listener on document with no removeEventListener guard, so a failure part-way through the body causes Ctrl+F / Ctrl+H to execute the find/replace command once per accumulated listener. The listener is also never disposed, so it leaks for the life of the page.
bugs.proposed_fix: Register the document listener exactly once. Hoist a `protected documentReloadHandler?: (e: KeyboardEvent) => void;` guard, add it at most once (e.g. at the top of onStart, or guard with `if (!this.documentReloadHandler)`), store the handler, and remove it in a `dispose()`/`onStop()` via `document.removeEventListener('keydown', handler, true)`. Also cap the readiness retry (a fixed number of attempts or an exponential backoff with a stop) so a missing StandaloneKeybindingService cannot spin a 1s timer forever.
bugs.evidence: Code path: line 60 and line 131 both re-enter registerEditorKeybindings; the listener at line 109 is added on every successful entry; no removeEventListener exists in the file.

bugs.bug: Backup capture never clears a stale backup for a widget it cannot read. In the `!control || !model` branch the code asks decideBackupAction({enabled:true, dirty, tooLarge:false}), but with matchesBackup/matchesFile omitted that function returns 'skip' when the buffer is clean and 'snapshot' when it is dirty - it can never return 'clear'. So the `=== 'clear'` branch is dead, and a saved-but-unreadable widget (or one whose editor was torn down) keeps its old snapshot indefinitely, which can then be restored over newer content.
bugs.proposed_fix: Decide explicitly for the unreadable case instead of calling the full policy: if the widget is clean, `await this.remove(key)` (drop the stale snapshot) and return; if it is dirty, keep the existing snapshot (leave it in place) and return. Drop the always-false `decideBackupAction(...) === 'clear'` condition, and add a unit-tested helper (e.g. clearUnreadableBackup(dirty)) to backup.ts so the rule is covered.
bugs.evidence: common/backup.ts:107-114 - with matchesBackup/matchesFile undefined the only returns are 'skip' (clean) and 'snapshot'/'clear' from the dirty branch, and tooLarge is hard-coded false.

bugs.bug: wrapLine loops forever (and then throws) when width <= 0. With width 0, `rest.length > 0` is true, slice(0,0) is '', lastIndexOf(' ') is -1, and the else branch pushes '' then sets rest = rest.slice(0) = rest, so the loop never advances; the out array grows until V8 throws 'Invalid array length'. Verified. The default is 80 and the UI passes 80, so this only fires if a caller ever forwards 0 or a negative wrap width.
bugs.proposed_fix: Guard the width at the top of wrapLine: `const columns = width > 0 ? Math.floor(width) : SPLIT_COLUMN;` and use `columns` throughout, so a non-positive width degrades to the default instead of looping. Add a test asserting wrapLine('hello', 0) does not hang.

bugs.bug: The Run output cap can overshoot MAX_OUTPUT. `if (output.length < MAX_OUTPUT) output += String(chunk);` appends a whole chunk whenever the buffer is currently under the cap, so a single large chunk (or the chunk that crosses the boundary) can push output past 64 KB by up to the chunk size. The buffer is meant to be a hard 64 KB cap.
bugs.proposed_fix: Clip to the cap: `if (output.length < MAX_OUTPUT) { output += String(chunk); if (output.length > MAX_OUTPUT) { output = output.slice(0, MAX_OUTPUT); } }` (or compute the remaining budget and slice the chunk). Consider appending a '\n… output truncated' marker once.
bugs.evidence: MAX_OUTPUT = 64 * 1024 at line 5; the guard is a pre-check only.

bugs.bug: The '*' entry in C_HASH_COMMENTS makes isCommentLine skip ANY line whose first non-space character is '*'. For C/C++/JavaScript/TypeScript that also skips real code such as a continued pointer expression or a line beginning with a dereference (`*ptr = foo;`), and for JS a generator method header (`*gen() {}`). It is a copying of Notepad++'s block-comment heuristic; the failure is silent (a symbol simply does not appear in the Function List).
bugs.proposed_fix: Only treat a leading '*' as a comment when the document is actually inside a block comment. Either track a simple `/* ... */` open/close state across lines in parseFunctionList and consult it, or narrow the prefix to '*/' and a line that is exactly '*'/'* ' (i.e. require the '*' to be followed by whitespace), rather than every line beginning with '*'. Amend the parser comment to state the chosen rule.
bugs.evidence: C_HASH_COMMENTS = ['//', '/*', '*'] at line 263; isCommentLine (lines 374-377) tests trimmed.startsWith('*').
